recognize_zh: 箭頭指的紅血球內血紅素濃縮成邊緣平直、有稜角的深色結晶塊，周圍留下淡染的空殼，形狀像手套或指狀突起，這就是 HbSC 結晶；背景還有許多靶形紅血球（target cells）。
features: Red cells with dense, straight-edged, angular hemoglobin crystals protruding from the cell (arrows)
Crystals leave pale, hemoglobin-poor cytoplasm in the rest of the cell; one has a glove/finger-like shape
Numerous target cells and folded cells in the background
No classic thin sickle cells in this field; platelets adequate
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows scattered red cells containing dense, straight-edged, angular hemoglobin crystals that bulge from the cell outline, leaving the remaining cytoplasm pale (arrows); one crystal-containing cell has a glove-like shape. The background shows numerous target cells and folded forms, while classic elongated sickle cells are not seen in this field. Findings are consistent with hemoglobin SC disease; hemoglobin HPLC or electrophoresis should confirm HbS and HbC.

ddx.vs: HbC crystals in HbCC are hexagonal or rod-shaped with parallel sides, with many target cells and spherocytes, and without finger-like SC crystal projections.
HbSS shows many thin, crescent sickle cells with pointed ends rather than blunt, angular crystals.

ddx.dx: Irregularly contracted cells or fragmented red cells
ddx.vs: Contracted cells and schistocytes are uniformly dense throughout without a crystal inside a pale ghost of residual membrane.
